title: Willowbrook Ward Conference Story Challenge
status: Implemented in Conference Story Challenge with retellings, reviewed clips, source speaker cards, and topic icons. Questions and answer criteria remain supported by the caption review.

topics.label: Follow Christ
topics.question: What blessings or results can we expect by following Him every day?

topics.label: Know Your Worth
topics.question: How does knowing who we are change how we see ourselves and treat others?

topics.label: Find Guidance
topics.question: How can we seek, recognize, and act on guidance from the Spirit?

topics.label: Find Strength
topics.question: What can we do when life is hard or our faith is strained?

topics.label: Keep Promises
topics.question: How do our covenants connect us to Jesus Christ and help us become more like Him?

topics.label: Help Others
topics.question: How can we help others feel the Savior's love?

scoring: All teams respond. Full value for a complete correct answer; half for a substantially correct incomplete multi-part answer; zero for incorrect or unsupported. No negative points, speed bonus, steals, or wagers.

cards.title: Peaches at the farm stand
cards.question: What fruit was one farm stand from Stevenson's childhood known for?
answerCriteria: Peaches.

cards.title: A plan that helped him stay
cards.question: What plan did the new missionary make with his trainer, and what changed later?
answerCriteria: A scripture-study plan, especially the Book of Mormon.
He understood his purpose, felt happier, and wanted to stay.

cards.title: Act well thy part
cards.question: A student has a small role in a school project and thinks it does not matter. Apply McKay's lesson with one specific action.
answerCriteria: Do the assigned part as well as possible.
Name a concrete action: prepare, finish honestly, help the group, or a comparable example.

cards.title: The missing promotion
cards.question: A friend says obedience must bring the outcome they want. Identify the mistaken expectation and suggest a better response using this story.
answerCriteria: Obedience does not guarantee a particular promotion or our preferred timetable.
Notice other help or blessings while honestly acknowledging disappointment.

cards.title: A name that changes our actions
cards.question: Explain the difference between adding Christ's name as a label and taking His name through covenant. Give a realistic action that shows the second.
answerCriteria: A label alone does not mean becoming like Christ.
Covenant discipleship involves an ongoing determination to serve Him.
Give a specific act of faithful or loving service linked to the teaching.

cards.title: The baby pictures
cards.question: What had the children done as babies to earn their parents' love?
answerCriteria: Nothing; their parents already loved them.

cards.title: More than hello
cards.question: What does I see you communicate beyond a greeting? Name two meanings.
answerCriteria: Any two: recognition, respect, human worth, concern, belonging, or you matter.

cards.title: The right location
cards.question: How does the GPS experience illustrate the Lord's knowledge of us? What does she say about Him knowing our weaknesses?
answerCriteria: The Lord knows where we actually are and our circumstances, unlike the confused GPS.
Knowing our weaknesses and questions does not make Him love us less.

cards.title: Everyone except me?
cards.question: A friend thinks God's promises apply to everyone except them. What did Linda learn, and how could her experience help you respond to your friend?
answerCriteria: Challenge the imagined personal exclusion: God's promises apply to them too.
Offer support, trust, or a faithful step while respecting the promises' conditions and God's timing.

cards.title: Love before improvement
cards.question: Your friend made a mistake and calls themself worthless. Use Christ's response to write two sentences supporting both worth and growth.
answerCriteria: Affirm worth and being known and loved without requiring perfection.
Encourage a constructive next step or repair without shame.
Connect to Christ's love preceding His invitation to improve.

cards.title: The kitchen table
cards.question: What did Caussé feel prompted to open after praying?
answerCriteria: The church magazine on his kitchen table.

cards.title: Look again
cards.question: What prompting interrupted Farnes's reading, and what did he do next?
answerCriteria: Look again at the anxious missionary.
Ask whether he was okay and begin helping.

cards.title: Find lift
cards.question: Use one detail from glider training for each step—seek, recognize, act—then give one spiritual application.
answerCriteria: Seek: learn from a trained guide or look for cues.
Recognize: notice the effect of unseen lift.
Act: turn into it and stay with it.
A reasonable parallel involving seeking guidance, attending to the Spirit, and acting faithfully.

cards.title: Scripture in a disagreement
cards.question: Name his source of guidance and how he recognized help. Suggest one action for a disagreement today; distinguish your suggestion from what the story actually reports.
answerCriteria: Christ's scriptural teaching against contention came to mind.
His mind was enlightened and he knew how to address the challenge.
Suggest a peaceful action such as pausing, apologizing, or listening; the exact reconciliation steps are not reported.

cards.title: The prompting was to wait
cards.question: Explain why waiting could be acting on a prompting even when time was short. Give a listening plan for a difficult conversation.
answerCriteria: The prompting asked for restraint rather than immediate speech, and he followed it.
Listening helped him understand people and teach from love.
A plan with attentive listening, a sincere question or summary, and a thoughtful response.

cards.title: Breakfast after recovery
cards.question: Which two breakfast details bothered the recovering patient?
answerCriteria: The oatmeal was not hot; the milk was not cold.

cards.title: Help before everything was fixed
cards.question: What two kinds of help did the family receive after the crash?
answerCriteria: Peace or assurance from the Spirit.
Practical assistance from other people.

cards.title: The missing box picture
cards.question: Why would Jack follow instructions without seeing the finished picture? Connect that with hope.
answerCriteria: He trusted the designer.
We can keep taking faithful steps without knowing the complete outcome.

cards.title: The master's deeper cuts
cards.question: Why did the sculptor need help, and what did the finished eyes teach about receiving it?
answerCriteria: He could not make the eyes lifelike alone and had to ask humbly.
The skilled instructor shaped what he could not, while the sculpture remained uniquely his.
Connect to receiving Christ's help and growth beyond our present ability.

cards.title: The last ten miles
cards.question: Explain two ways Ted helped without shortening the race. Use that pattern for a practical support plan for a discouraged friend.
answerCriteria: Ted quietly carried Dunn's hydration pack and two water bottles through the last ten miles.
He encouraged Dunn and stayed patiently beside him so he could keep going.
A plan with emotional support and a useful practical action, without promising the challenge disappears.

cards.title: A first covenant step
cards.question: Which ordinance did the two great-grandchildren choose?
answerCriteria: Baptism.

cards.title: A small building
cards.question: What did Gong say is not big or small even if the temple building is small?
answerCriteria: Ordinances and covenants; their spiritual blessings are not measured by building size.

cards.title: A gift for their mother
cards.question: How did the children support their mother's worship? What does this show about helping someone keep covenants?
answerCriteria: Saved to buy her own temple clothing.
Practical sacrifice and loving support can help someone worship and live their commitments.

cards.title: Consider your ways
cards.question: What priority changed in Haggai's account? According to Schmeil, what are we asked to build today?
answerCriteria: The people prioritized rebuilding the temple in response to God.
A strong relationship with Heavenly Father and Christ through making and keeping covenants.

cards.title: A useful analogy—with a limit
cards.question: Give two connections between the passport story and covenants. Then state the important limit Bednar gives.
answerCriteria: Receiving credentials and ongoing care or faithfulness both matter.
The authorized stamp parallels a verifying witness; possession alone is insufficient.
Hardships or injuries suffered through no fault of our own do not invalidate our covenants or God's promises.

cards.title: A tiny helping hand
cards.question: How did the girl help the boy during the Primary program?
answerCriteria: Unbuttoned his sleeve from the lapel so he could move freely.

cards.title: Under the mango tree
cards.question: What does Reid most remember about his Primary teachers? Name two details.
answerCriteria: Their love.
They knew the children personally and by name.

cards.title: Your daughter sees me
cards.question: Name two things the student did for the janitor. Explain how they helped him feel Christ's love.
answerCriteria: Any two: greeted him, knew his name, helped clean after lunch.
Showed recognition, dignity, and practical care.

cards.title: How are you really doing?
cards.question: Why did the second question matter? Name two helpful actions another person could also take.
answerCriteria: It made room for an honest answer beyond the forced smile.
Any two: listened, appreciated, encouraged, helped with the concern, or offered appropriate warmth.

cards.title: Repair the reply
cards.question: A friend criticizes your beliefs. Write a response holding a conviction with love. Explain how it improves on the angry retort.
answerCriteria: Express a belief clearly and calmly.
Ask or listen to understand, avoiding insult or shame.
Explain that helping the person and preserving charity matter more than winning the debate.
